title: Mono- and diglycerides, 21 CFR 184.1505: direct food substances affirmed as generally recognized as safe
journal: Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, section 184.1505, read in the electronic Code of Federal Regulations, title 21 amended to 14 October 2026
funder: US Food and Drug Administration; the text is federal regulation codified by the Office of the Federal Register.
result: Mono- and diglycerides consist of a mixture of glyceryl mono- and diesters, and minor amounts of triesters, prepared from fats or oils or fat-forming acids derived from edible sources; the most prevalent fatty acids include lauric, linoleic, myristic, oleic, palmitic and stearic. They are manufactured by the reaction of glycerin with fatty acids or with triglycerides in the presence of an alkaline catalyst and purified to a mixture of glycerides, free fatty acids and free glycerin containing at least 90 percent-by-weight glycerides, meeting the Food Chemicals Codex, 3rd edition (1981), p. 201. In accordance with 184.1(b)(1) the ingredient is used in food with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice; the GRAS affirmation rests on use as a dough strengthener, emulsifier and emulsifier salt, flavoring agent and adjuvant, formulation aid, lubricant and release agent, solvent and vehicle, stabilizer and thickener, surface-active agent, surface-finishing agent and texturizer at levels not exceeding current good manufacturing practice. Source: 54 FR 7403, 21 February 1989, as amended at 57 FR 10616, 27 March 1992.
